items.headline: Truemed CEO Justin Mares Explains Why HSAs are Having a ‘Break-Out Moment’
items.summary: In this NYSE Live interview, Justin Mares, CEO of TruMed, discusses how Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) are evolving beyond traditional healthcare spending and increasingly supporting preventative wellness initiatives. Mares begins by outlining the differences between HSAs and FSAs and explains why both accounts have become important tools for consumers seeking tax advantages while managing healthcare-related expenses. A significant portion of the discussion focuses on the growing popularity of preventative healthcare. Rather than waiting for medical issues to emerge, many consumers are proactively investing in fitness, exercise, sleep optimization, and health-monitoring technologies that support long-term wellbeing. The interview also explores changing consumer behavior. Mares explains that increased awareness around chronic disease prevention, healthcare costs, and overall wellness is prompting more individuals to evaluate how they use healthcare savings vehicles. Another major theme is the rise of health technology. Wearable devices, smart fitness tools, recovery systems, and sleep-tracking solutions are giving consumers new ways to monitor their health and make data-driven lifestyle decisions. Mares discusses how these technologies are helping people take a more active role in managing their wellbeing. The conversation further examines demand trends within TruMed's marketplace. According to Mares, fitness-related products and services remain among the most popular categories as consumers prioritize exercise and preventative care as key components of their health strategies. The interview also addresses open enrollment planning and consumer awareness. Mares encourages individuals to understand available benefits and evaluate how tax-advantaged healthcare accounts can support both current and future wellness needs. Looking forward, Mares believes increasing awareness, continued innovation in health technology, and growing interest in preventative medicine will contribute to further growth across the health savings ecosystem. Throughout the discussion, Mares shares perspectives on healthcare, preventative wellness, HSAs, FSAs, fitness technology, consumer health trends, financial wellness, open enrollment planning, and the future of personalized healthcare.
